kept.heading: THE GREAT DIGITAL FATIGUE: HOW DIGITAL BURNOUT IS CHANGING SOCIAL MEDIA USE (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Users are pulling back from social media, with 55% posting less and 53% limiting audiences, while 47% have deleted apps due to stress. Over half say maintaining a presence feels like work, especially Gen Z, and 44% cite political content as a reason to disengage. Stepping away brings mixed emotions, with 27% feeling peaceful but 22% anxious, highlighting how platforms now feel more like obligations than connection.

kept.heading: THE FORTUNE 500 IS DELETING THE CMO TITLE (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The CMO title is disappearing, with only 36% of Fortune 500 companies still using it, down from 49% last year. Companies are folding marketing into revenue and growth roles, and fewer marketing leaders report to the CEO, now at 52%. Roles like Chief Growth Officer and Chief Commercial Officer are replacing CMOs, as companies push for direct revenue ownership. The role isn't disappearing, but being absorbed into broader functions.

kept.heading: 5 STORYTELLING FRAMEWORKS TO ATTRACT B2B BUYERS (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A B2B narrative is not an emotional pitch but a logical thread connecting why a brand exists, what it's fighting against, and how it helps customers win. Each event in that story needs to happen because of the one before it, replacing the flat "and then" of a feature list with a "because of that" chain that creates stakes and payoff. That thread also needs an opponent, the specific practice or belief the brand positions itself against, since without one there's nothing for the story to resolve.

kept.heading: HOW TO BUILD A BRAND PRESENCE ON REDDIT IN 2026 (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Reddit works best when brands learn community behavior before they try to promote anything. Start by using the free Reddit Pro tools to track keywords, analyze discussions, and monitor performance. Spend time in relevant subreddits to understand the tone and common conversations so your organic posts and ads match community expectations. Reddit has become more valuable because Google Search and AI chatbots cite its discussions more often, so a strong presence can increase product discovery and brand visibility.

kept.heading: VIDEO EDITING WITH CLAUDE: 5 AI SKILLS YOU NEED TO TRY (34 MINUTE VIDEO)
kept.blurb: This video shows how to use Claude to cut videos with transcript-based edits, add auto-zooms, organize assets with a Slack bot, apply AI color grading, and find B-roll from across the web. The workflow uses Claude, GitHub skills, MCPs, and tools like Tela to automate repetitive editing tasks.

kept.heading: IF YOUR BRAND ISN'T SHOWING UP IN YOUTUBE AI SEARCH, YOUR COMPETITORS ARE (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google's AI search is pulling YouTube videos into answers, often favoring creators over brands. Content that's clearly structured and built around real questions performs best. Depth across related topics also matters more than single keywords. Creators are winning by doing this well, leaving brands that rely on product-led content at risk of being left out of the answer.

kept.heading: FUNNY MARKETING 101 (18 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Effective marketing humor comes down to two rules that don't apply to comedy in general, being specific enough that only a narrow audience gets the joke, and being surprising enough to subvert what that audience already expects. Niche recognition works because most brands never bother creating humor built for one audience's daily frustrations, which is why an internal joke about IT teams or LinkedIn cringe can outperform anything broader. The same subversion shows up in a simple format, one where a familiar structure gets a new idea poured into it, then twisted in a way the audience doesn't see coming.

kept.heading: SUBSTACK'S NEW TOOL TELLS YOU WHO'S BEEN WRITING THEIR NEWSLETTERS WITH AI (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Substack is integrating AI detection software from Pangram so readers can see an estimated human-versus-AI split for any newsletter post, note, or comment over 100 characters.

kept.heading: HOW POPPI BUILT A BILLION-DOLLAR SODA BRAND (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Poppi created its own category, then spent roughly 20% of its marketing budget on TikTok creators, making creator content the primary driver of awareness.

kept.heading: CORPORATE AMERICA HAS SUDDENLY DECIDED TO STOP BLOWING MONEY ON AI (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Companies are cutting AI costs by mixing models instead of relying solely on premium providers like OpenAI and Anthropic. Businesses are using cheaper open-weight models for routine tasks while reserving advanced models for complex work. Cursor found a hybrid approach reduced a browser-building experiment from $10K to $1.3K, showing how companies are optimizing AI spending with flexible model choices.

kept.heading: THE CREATOR ECONOMY HAS A NEW MIDDLE CLASS (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Microinfluencers have become a more cost-effective advertising channel because loyal niche audiences often deliver stronger engagement at a lower price than large creators. Microinfluencers average a 3.2% engagement rate versus 1.1% for macroinfluencers. Brands now hire many smaller creators instead of a few large ones to get better returns from the same budget. The creator economy has grown to a projected $33B in 2025 as affiliate links, brand deals, and storefronts give creators multiple ways to earn revenue.

kept.heading: PERSONALITY ON REDDIT MATTERS MORE THAN YOU THINK (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Branded persona accounts can build more trust on Reddit than logo-based accounts by participating authentically. Treat the account as a long-term GEO asset by tracking search visibility, LLM citations, and referral traffic, not just karma. Annuity.org's persona account earned 100 karma and 11 LLM-cited threads in two months. Brands should spend 2 to 4 weeks observing communities before posting, as genuine conversations outperform polished promotions.

kept.heading: DOES DOMAIN AGE AFFECT EMAIL OPEN RATES? (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Older email domains tend to earn higher open rates than newer ones. Domains aged 1 to 2 years averaged 21.6% opens vs 34.9% for 5 to 6 year domains, even with proper authentication. Domain age appears linked to sender reputation, so new domains should focus on targeted outreach to build trust over time.

kept.heading: HOW ONE CHANGE WAS WORTH MILLIONS MORE FOR A MAJOR AIRLINE (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Changing a default setting can increase conversions when it matches what customers want most. A major low-cost airline changed its flight results from departure time first to lowest price first because its customers usually choose the airline to save money. The test increased bookings by 1.1%, which could add millions in annual revenue on a site with millions of travelers. Review every default in your website or app because small interface choices can influence customer decisions.

kept.heading: THE TOP CAUSE OF WASTED AD SPEND (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Poor tracking data is the biggest cause of wasted ad spend because ad platforms optimize campaigns based on the data they receive. Tracking errors such as duplicate tags and inflated conversion counts can cause advertisers to spend money on the wrong outcomes even if the creative and targeting are strong. Audit your tracking setup regularly and fix data quality issues before optimizing ads or landing pages. Brands spending about $80K per month on ads can often justify third-party tracking tools for incremental improvements after the core setup is accurate.

kept.heading: COCA-COLA JUST REBRANDED. THE MOST SURPRISING PART IS WHAT IT DIDN'T CHANGE (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Coca-Cola refreshed its brand by doubling down on iconic assets, reinforcing familiar visuals instead of reinventing to keep recognition strong.

kept.heading: LIBRARIANS ARE HOSTING VIRAL ‘AVOIDING AI' WORKSHOPS FOR PEOPLE WHO ARE FED UP WITH BIG TECH (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Librarians are teaching people to disable AI features, reflecting frustration with forced adoption and demand for more control.

kept.heading: HOW B2B UNPLUGGED BUILT A SOLD-OUT EVENT SERIES BY FIXING WHAT CONFERENCES GET WRONG (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: B2B Unplugged built sold-out events by ditching panels for curated, small-group discussions.
